nine_requested_scientific_checks.question: Model input and output dimensions
nine_requested_scientific_checks.finding: Captured model accepts image tensors plus caption text. Image loader uses RGB images; transformation details are delegated to uncaptured get_transforms. nine_requested_scientific_checks.finding: A linear image classifier is separate from a convolutional mask head with one output channel by default. Training explicitly includes mask_head parameters and a mask loss. This is positive evidence for a learned mask branch.

nine_requested_scientific_checks.question: Pixel, patch, mask or region predictions
nine_requested_scientific_checks.finding: Visual patch tokens are reshaped to a spatial map, passed through the mask head, and bilinearly upsampled to 224x224. Raw mask logits are returned alongside class logits.

nine_requested_scientific_checks.question: Whether spatial predictions represent AI-generated/edited content
nine_requested_scientific_checks.finding: The identity-matched abstract describes localization of manipulated regions, and the repository loads a separate mask_label path. nine_requested_scientific_checks.finding: Existing mask files are loaded as grayscale targets. Training uses a validity flag when a mask path exists and substitutes a zero target with false validity when absent. Evaluation also substitutes zero masks for absent paths. Annotation origin, correctness, binarization/transform behavior, sample counts and forensic interpretation cannot be established without the full protocol or dataset metadata.
nine_requested_scientific_checks.bounds: No target mask, CSV dataset payload or image was downloaded or inspected.

No executed outputs, paper spatial table values or localization-baseline comparison were obtained.

nine_requested_scientific_checks.question: Segmentation outputs evaluated against ground-truth masks
nine_requested_scientific_checks.finding: The evaluator compares binarized predicted masks with loaded target masks and calculates TP/FP/FN. It includes only samples whose target mask sum is positive. This establishes a coded comparison path, not proof that the target paper quantitatively reported it under an identified split/baseline protocol.
nine_requested_scientific_checks.bounds: Code not executed; positive-mask filtering excludes empty-target examples from the spatial metric aggregate.

Therefore an attention-only or no-spatial-output description would contradict available code. The missing published GT/protocol/numerical evidence still prevents a confident T2 task-addition proposal.

eight_requested_checks.question: Are real images included in the prediction label space?
eight_requested_checks.answer: Yes. Section3.1 defines a finite source-ground-truth set consisting of pretrained GAN instances plus the real world. Table1 explicitly uses five classes: real, ProGAN, SNGAN, CramerGAN and MMDGAN.

eight_requested_checks.question: Is a real-versus-GAN decision rule explicitly defined?
eight_requested_checks.answer: The paper repeatedly states that it distinguishes real and generated images, and a real source can be predicted by the source classifier. It does not specify a separate binary head, a real-versus-sum-of-GAN score, threshold, source-collapse rule or distinct two-stage real/fake decision protocol. The operationally specified output is a source label from finiteY.

eight_requested_checks.question: Is genuine authenticity detection quantitatively evaluated?
eight_requested_checks.answer: No independently scored authenticity endpoint was found in the complete main paper. The reported classification accuracies evaluate correctness of the exact source label, including real as one source. Such joint correctness is not a separately measured real/fake metric.

eight_requested_checks.question: Are detection results separated from generator-attribution results?
eight_requested_checks.answer: No. There is no separate detection table, binary ROC/PR curve, authenticity confusion table or binary subgroup result. Tables1–8 retain source-attribution settings; FD ratios quantify feature separation across source classes.

eight_requested_checks.question: Are real images treated as another source class?
eight_requested_checks.answer: Yes in the defined and evaluated classifier. A real-source label is trained alongside GAN instance labels. The authors also motivate visual-forensics use, so describing this as a mere absence of a real/GAN claim would be inaccurate; the distinction is claim/joint capability versus independent detection evaluation.

eight_requested_checks.question: Would generator-ID accuracy be incorrectly reused as detection accuracy?
eight_requested_checks.answer: Yes if the joint-source scores were relabeled as binary accuracy. A ProGAN→SNGAN error is an attribution error while leaving binary generated status unchanged. A real→GAN error changes authenticity. The aggregate source accuracy does not supply the full binary error breakdown, and no binary score is derived here.

eight_requested_checks.question: Are binary accuracy, ROC/AUC, F1 or equivalent authenticity-specific measures reported?
eight_requested_checks.answer: None found for the proposed forensic classifier in the main paper. Accuracy percentages are exact source-class accuracy; FD ratio is an inter-/intra-source Fréchet distance ratio. No ROC/AUC, F1, authenticity AP or real-class sensitivity/specificity/operating point is provided.

eight_requested_checks.question: Are separate detection operating points or protocols evaluated?
eight_requested_checks.answer: None found. The experiments vary source architecture, GAN training data, initialization seed, frequency band, effective patch size, perceptual selection and perturbation immunization while retaining attribution labels. These variations do not create an independently measured binary protocol.

method_and_label_space.main_output: A finite source class fromY: known pretrained GAN instances plus the real world. Figure2’s terminal output is #labels, preceded by a1x1x512 representation.
method_and_label_space.model_fingerprint: The corresponding1x1x512 weights of the final fully connected source classifier for a GAN instance.
method_and_label_space.main_loss: Figure2 caption specifies cross-entropy classification loss over image-source ground truth.
method_and_label_space.architecture_variants: Pre-downsampling, residual frequency-band extraction and post-pooling alter source-fingerprint evidence. Even patch-statistics variants end in a source prediction; they do not supply a separate forensic localization or detection output.
method_and_label_space.visualization_network: Section3.3 learns an autoencoder reconstructionR(I), image residual fingerprintR(I)-I and trainable model fingerprint per source. Correlation with each source fingerprint supplies the class logits. This variant is explicitly for visualization/interpretation and has extra complexity.
method_and_label_space.visualization_objective: Eqs1–4 combine pixel L1 reconstruction, reconstruction adversarial regularization with gradient penalty, and source-ground-truth classification; weights20.0,0.1,1.0. No independent binary authenticity objective or evaluation is added by those terms.
method_and_label_space.discriminator_boundary: D_rec in Eq2 is a reconstruction adversarial critic, not a reported real-versus-GAN forensic head. Original GAN discriminators are discussed as using unaligned embedding spaces; the evaluated external network predicts sources.
method_and_label_space.service_authenticity_boundary: The last paragraph of Sec3.1 uses authenticity to mean membership in a desired GAN API/service and service identity by majority source prediction. That is source/model verification, not a separately scored camera-real-versus-generated protocol.

experimental_protocol.reported_dataset_size: Sec4.1 p5 states20,000 real-world RGB images for each dataset.
experimental_protocol.GANs: ProGAN, SNGAN, CramerGAN and MMDGAN; trained from scratch with defaults except240epochs and128x128x3 output size.
experimental_protocol.architecture_source_experiment: Table1:5-way real+4GAN architecture classification. Sec4.2 states100,000 images per source for classifier training and10,000 per source for testing.
experimental_protocol.training_set_source_experiment: A100,000-image real base subset and10other100,000-image subsets are constructed. The listed replacement counts are1,10,100,1000,10000,20000,40000,60000,80000,100000. ProGAN instances trained on varied subsets are treated as distinct attribution sources; Table2 aggregates attribution results. The prose/table notation does not supply a separate binary result per replacement count. No exact total class-count assumption is required here.
experimental_protocol.seed_source_experiment: Table3: real plus10ProGAN instances trained with different initialization seeds on the entire real dataset; hence11source classes. Paper reports100,000 train and10,000 test images in that sampling setup. Two identically seeded instances are reported indistinguishable at random attribution chance as a sanity check.
experimental_protocol.frequency_patch_experiments: Tables4–5 reuse real+seed-instance source labels; vary frequency components and effective local receptive fields while still reporting global source accuracy.
experimental_protocol.high_quality_subset: Table6 selects the10%test-generated images most perceptually similar to the real dataset via1-nearest-neighbor perceptual similarity. The classifier was trained on non-selected images. This is the authors’ artifact-bias probe, not independent proof that every selected image is artifact-free.
experimental_protocol.perturbation_experiments: Tables7–8 use the real+ProGANseed label set. Atk measures the pretrained source classifier under perturbation; Dfs measures attack-category-aware fine-tuning.
experimental_protocol.known_source_boundary: All reported source experiments concern known source classes/instances. Changed GAN architecture/data/seed is a source distinction trained for attribution, not a demonstrated held-out-generator authenticity test.
experimental_protocol.sample_count_inconsistency: The visually verified20,000-real-image dataset statement conflicts with later100,000-image real subsets and100,000train+10,000test images per real source. The main paper does not explain this discrepancy; do not silently rewrite20,000 as200,000 or infer sampling with replacement.

quantitative_results.metric_boundary: All accuracy values below are percentages of source-class attribution correctness as defined in Sec4.1. They are not separately reported binary real/fake accuracies. FD ratios are source-feature separation statistics, not detector operating points.

Table2_p6_printed7561.label_set: real plus ProGAN_subset_diff#i sources; multiple data-overlap variants, not a standalone binary source pair result.

Figure7_p8_printed7563.finding: A visualization of real/CelebA and example ProGAN image/model fingerprint interactions, with strongest interaction for matching source. It is not an aggregate binary detection confusion matrix or an ROC/operating-point result.

attack_details.noise: Add iidGaussian noise with variance drawn fromU[5.0,20.0] as reported; intensity normalization is not specified.
attack_details.blur: Gaussian filtering with kernel chosen from1,3,5,7,9.
attack_details.cropping: Random offset5%–20%ofimage side lengths, then resize to original dimensions.
attack_details.relighting: SfSNet changes the illumination condition to a sampled condition.
attack_details.boundary: Attack/defense rows retain source accuracy. They are not independent binary detector threshold sweeps.

contradictions_and_limitations.finding: The authors explicitly claim using fingerprints to classify real versus generated content and interpret Table1 as differentiating real/GAN and attributing sources. This is positive contrary evidence to any blanket statement that authenticity is never considered. The measured main-paper protocol is still a single finite-source task; it does not give a separately scored detection endpoint.

A real source in a multiway output could enable a derived real/anyGAN decision, but that derivation and its binary errors/operating point are not reported. No such metric is calculated or invented during this review.

The real/ProGAN_subset_diff#i notation represents a family of source variants with one aggregate score per dataset. The main paper does not present per-i binary detection values or an explicit binary authenticity metric. An uncertain exact Table2 class count does not create positive evidence of a binary protocol.
The service-authenticity discussion is desired-source verification, not separately measured camera-real-versus-generated detection.
Visually confirmed20,000realimages per dataset is inconsistent with later100,000-image subsets and100,000/10,000classifier source sampling. The discrepancy is retained, not corrected by inference.

The main paper references external supplementary material for additional figures and FD-ratio details. It was not retrieved under the one-main-manuscript budget. The conclusion is bounded to complete official main-paper evidence, not an assertion about every unretrieved artifact.
This is the official ICCV2019 main paper. No arXiv version comparison, code reproduction, author rename, metadata correction or independent research-type review is performed.

terminal_decision.title: Attributing Fake Images to GANs: Learning and Analyzing GAN Fingerprints
terminal_decision.review_note: Batch B review T631; SUPPORTED_NO_CHANGE. Maintainer accepted retaining tasks source_attribution -> source_attribution for curated:170f07b3d7020611e566 under locked T1. The complete official ICCV 2019 proceedings main paper defines multiclass source-identity prediction over GAN instances plus a real-world source class. Table 1 reports five-way attribution accuracy 99.43% on CelebA and 98.58% on LSUN; Table 3 reports attribution accuracy 99.14% and 97.04% for real images plus ten ProGAN instances. These are multiclass attribution scores, not binary detection accuracies. Main-paper review established no separately defined and independently evaluated binary real-versus-generated detection protocol, authenticity-specific metric or operating-point analysis. The paper claims that its real-inclusive classifier differentiates generated images from real ones, but that claim and desired-service authenticity discussion do not supply an independent binary evaluation. Preserve source_attribution, method, fully_generated, all canonical bibliography, authors, affiliations and relationships. Do not add detection or alter task compatibility fields. Evidence: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_ICCV_2019/papers/Yu_Attributing_Fake_Images_to_GANs_Learning_and_Analyzing_GAN_Fingerprints_ICCV_2019_paper.pdf; official eleven-page ICCV main paper, printed pages 7556-7566, SHA256 be717607d2204d42d4a8e96f092bcbbef4e749a43df587bd9e0940afea5cebea. The conclusion is bounded to this reviewed main paper; no separate supplement, code, model/data payload or alternate arXiv version was reviewed. This resolves only the original T631 task-taxonomy action. T046 remains EVIDENCE_STILL_INSUFFICIENT and open; all independent questions and original pending-review evidence remain unchanged. Approved no-change disposition is recorded; no further action remains for this exact bounded review.

adjudication.main_paper_limitation: Complete official ICCV 2019 main paper only; supplementary contents and alternate versions unreviewed. Real-inclusive source classification and authors' real/GAN claims do not establish a separately evaluated binary authenticity endpoint.

terminal_decision.title: Attributing Fake Images to GANs: Learning and Analyzing GAN Fingerprints
terminal_decision.review_note: Batch B review T631; SUPPORTED_NO_CHANGE. Maintainer accepted retaining tasks source_attribution -> source_attribution for curated:170f07b3d7020611e566 under locked T1. The complete official ICCV 2019 proceedings main paper defines multiclass source-identity prediction over GAN instances plus a real-world source class. Table 1 reports five-way attribution accuracy 99.43% on CelebA and 98.58% on LSUN; Table 3 reports attribution accuracy 99.14% and 97.04% for real images plus ten ProGAN instances. These are multiclass attribution scores, not binary detection accuracies. Main-paper review established no separately defined and independently evaluated binary real-versus-generated detection protocol, authenticity-specific metric or operating-point analysis. The paper claims that its real-inclusive classifier differentiates generated images from real ones, but that claim and desired-service authenticity discussion do not supply an independent binary evaluation. Preserve source_attribution, method, fully_generated, all canonical bibliography, authors, affiliations and relationships. Do not add detection or alter task compatibility fields. Evidence: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_ICCV_2019/papers/Yu_Attributing_Fake_Images_to_GANs_Learning_and_Analyzing_GAN_Fingerprints_ICCV_2019_paper.pdf; official eleven-page ICCV main paper, printed pages 7556-7566, SHA256 be717607d2204d42d4a8e96f092bcbbef4e749a43df587bd9e0940afea5cebea. The conclusion is bounded to this reviewed main paper; no separate supplement, code, model/data payload or alternate arXiv version was reviewed. This resolves only the original T631 task-taxonomy action. T046 remains EVIDENCE_STILL_INSUFFICIENT and open; all independent questions and original pending-review evidence remain unchanged. Approved no-change disposition is recorded; no further action remains for this exact bounded review.

adjudication.main_paper_limitation: Complete official ICCV 2019 main paper only; supplementary contents and alternate versions unreviewed. Real-inclusive source classification and authors' real/GAN claims do not establish a separately evaluated binary authenticity endpoint.
